use-formulas.why: A formula is a stored relationship: substitute what you know and read off what you do not. Carrying the units through the substitution is what tells you whether the answer is sensible.
traps: Check the formula's assumptions. ~A = \f{1}{2}bh~ needs the height perpendicular to the base, not a slanted side.

rearrange-formulas.why: Solving for a different letter uses exactly the rules for solving a numerical equation — treat every other letter as though it were a number. This is the skill that turns one formula into every formula you need from it.
traps: Isolate the target letter completely. ~2x = y - b~ is not solved for ~x~ until you divide by 2.

formula-build.why: Writing your own formula is the real skill: a fixed amount becomes a constant, a per-unit amount multiplies the variable, and something being used up subtracts. Every pricing model, pay structure and depreciation schedule is built this way.
traps: Decide what each letter means and write it down. A formula without stated meanings cannot be checked by anyone, including you.
